name: Jörgen Elofsson
notes: The Cheiron-school topline writer for diva and talent-show pop — the "moment" ballad specialist. 66–96 for the ballads and 118–132 for the uptempos he writes into, both straight, so a single window carries 66–132. Like the other writers on this board the research is explicit that drums are "not his department — he writes to a piano/guitar demo, and the melodic rhythm assumes a 2&4 backbeat with **the hook landing on beat 1 of the chorus**". That last clause is what the drum block reads: the kit is a demo bed, so the kick is sparse on 1 and 3, the hat is 8th-weighted at a low fill density, and the accent tier is lifted on the downbeat-heavy side while the fills stay out of the way. His melodic signature is the model's reason to exist: "the **stepwise climb with a delayed apex** — the chorus rises scale-wise and holds the highest note on the title's stressed syllable; verses are conversational and low", which is a step share of 0.86, an arch-dominant contour and a low note density. Harmony is a I–V–vi–IV backbone for the ballads and "non-functional indie-derived cycles (e.g. I–ii–vi–IV)" on the pop-rock material — both authored. "His ballads always leave a 2-bar instrumental gap after the title for the string answer", which is the sustain-pad counter and the high `dropOutBeats`. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research rates it medium-high and says the harmonic specifics are partly inferred. ⚠ The whole drums block is **INFERRED** from the stated demo bed, as is `bpm.mode` 92. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“n/a — toplines stay above the bass register; the melody's lowest note is usually the tonic in the singer's middle register so the belt has headroom.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
